newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN HIGH LIQUIDITY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN HIGH LIQUIDITY.

text.p: Short-term trading rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted stable in high liquidity on Thursday in line with dealers' predictions.
"The only difference is that it's a slightly more active today, but the rates are holding steady and the market is very liquid from treasury bill maturities," one dealer said.
"We are not expecting much change," he added.
NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at Wednesay's 28 percent level and sold at an unchanged 22 percent while call money was quoted at its overnight 20 percent rate.
Bankers' acceptance bills (BAs) were being bought at 22 percent, also the same as overnight, and were selling at a stable 21 percent.
